debts.title: Your debts
debts.lede: The order you pay them in matters. Choose your method and the app splits the money for you.
debts.note.avalanche: You pay off the debt with the highest rate first. This is the method that costs the least interest.
debts.note.snowball: You pay off the smallest debt first. One debt disappears quickly, and that win helps you keep going.
debts.noCapacity: With your current plan, the money set aside each month is not enough to pay off your debts. Adjust your budget in the Plan tab.
debts.none: No debt entered. You can add one in the Plan tab.
compare.title: The two methods compared
compare.same: Both methods give almost the same result.
seasons.title: The big expenses of the year
seasons.lede: Ramadan, Eid, summer, back to school: these moments come back every year. Set a little aside every week so they stop breaking your budget and pushing you to borrow.
seasons.total: set aside for these moments. This amount is already deducted when your freedom date is calculated. At each new month, the app adds it to what you have already set aside.
seasons.note: ≈ Ramadan and Eid follow the lunar calendar. The dates are approximate: the exact day depends on the sighting of the crescent. You can correct them with “Edit”.
seasons.edit.title: Edit: {name}
plan.title: Your plan
plan.lede: Put your numbers here. Your freedom date and today's number are recalculated with every change.
plan.revenu.hint: Salary and other money coming in
plan.fixes.hint: Rent, bills, subscriptions. Without your debt payments.
plan.debt.name: Name of the debt
plan.debt.none: No debt. Add one to calculate your date.
plan.initial.hint: Used to calculate the percentage already paid off.
plan.how.1: Every month, what is left after your fixed costs, your living budget and the big expenses of the year goes to your debts.
plan.how.2: The interest on each debt is counted. After the minimum payments, the money goes first to the debt chosen by your method.
plan.how.3: Today's number is what is left of your living budget, shared between the days left in the month.
plan.how.4: Spending above your pace pushes the date back. A day when you spend less than planned brings it closer.
plan.how.5: When you skip a purchase, the amount leaves this month's budget and goes to your debt. The date moves up right away.
plan.how.6: At each new month, the app does the sums by itself: it adds the interest, takes off the month's payment and sets money aside for the big expenses.
plan.how.7: The app cannot see your bank account. What you do not write down counts as not spent, so as paid off. If your statement says otherwise, correct what is left to pay here.
